summary: Fumimasa Fukui was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Waseda University (~1954–1962) and at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Paul Demiéville (~1964–1968). He served as a professor at Waseda University (~1978–2004).
Fumio Enomoto is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a research assistant at Kyoto University (~1978–1984) and later as a professor at Osaka University (~1998–2017).

Fumio Masutani worked in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1946–1953), Shizuoka University (~1953–1960), Taisho University (~1960–1973), and Tsuru University.

Fumio Matsuda specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He held a post at Komazawa University and served as an executive committee chairman for the Association for the Study of Indian Religions (attested 1997).

Fumio Ouchi works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Otani University, where he also held posts as assistant professor (attested 1996) and professor (attested 2014).
Fumio Shoji is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University. He held an assistant post in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies at Rissho University (attested 2015).
Fumio Tamamuro is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Meiji University (~1954–1960) and later held a post there (~1972–2006).
Futoshi Omae works in Indology and philosophy. He served as a lecturer at Kyushu University (attested 1986–1991) and held a post at Shimane Prefectural Junior College (attested 1997).

Futoshi Takehashi works in Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral coursework at Otani University (attested 1992) and served as an assistant at the Shinshu Otani-ha Research Institute of Teaching (1995–1997).

Fyodor Shcherbatskoy was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Ivan Minayev and under Georg Bühler. He held a post at Saint Petersburg State University (~1900–1941).
Félix Nève was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Eugène Burnouf (~1839–1840) and Christian Lassen (~1840–1841). He was appointed professor at KU Leuven in 1841.
G. V. Aston is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies. Aston earned a PhD in philosophy at the University of Canterbury (1986–2004) under teacher Paul Harrison.

G. V. Devasthali was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Hari Damodar Velankar (attested 1944). He taught as professor of Sanskrit at H.P.T. Arts and R.Y.K. Science College and at Savitribai Phule Pune University.

Gadjin Nagao was a Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology scholar who studied at Kyoto University under Susumu Yamaguchi. He held the Chair of Buddhist Studies at Kyoto University (1935–1971) and taught at Kyushu University and Tekko Junior College.

Gail Hinich Sutherland works in religious studies and Indology. Sutherland studied at the University of Chicago under Carol Bolon, Wendy Doniger, and Frank E. Reynolds, and studied under Virendra Singh.

Gajanan Balkrishna Palsule is an Indologist and linguist. He served as a sub-editor at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1950) and held a post at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1987).

Gananath Obeyesekere was a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Washington (~1958–1964). He held posts at the University of California, San Diego (~1972–1980) and Princeton University (~1980–2000).

Ganganatha Jha was an Indology and philosophy scholar educated at University of Calcutta and University of Allahabad. He worked at Darbhanga Raj Library, Muir Central College as Sanskrit professor, and served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Allahabad.

Gangs zhun works in Tibetology. He studied at Hainan College for Nationalities until 1989 and completed a master's degree at Northwest Minzu University (1998–2001) under the supervision of Alak Dorje Rinpoche.

Ganzorig Davaa-Ochir is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Davaa-Ochir earned an M.Phil. in Tibetan Studies at the University of Oslo under Hanna Havnevik (attested 2008), having also studied under Lama Byambaa.
